answers.explanation: Looking things up for clients is the caching (recursive) server's job. An authoritative server answers only for its own zones.
A zone transfer can be big, and every record must arrive, so it uses TCP on port 53.
Every refresh interval it compares serials. Higher means changed.
A secondary has a full copy of the zone and answers with the AA flag, just like the primary.
It came from a cache, not from a server that runs the zone. nslookup prints "Non-authoritative answer".
If the only nameserver is down, the entire domain disappears from the Internet, even if the web and mail servers are fine.
Poison one cache and you redirect thousands of users without touching their machines.
Dynamic DNS lets DHCP and DNS work together, which you'll plan for in the project.
